Main case
By way of present appeal filed under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, (for short 'the Act')

vide its award dated 23.09.2014.

sentences.text: Counsel for the appellants submits that the claimants are the 1 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:002639 heirs of Bagga Ram, who was travelling on a Tata Truck and died when the vehicle fell in a ditch while saving an antelope, who came on the road.

Counsel for the appellants has asserted that the Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs. 4,58,300/- to the appellants, which is highly inadequate as the deceased was found to be 35 years of age and was earning Rs.3,300/- per month as a labourer.
They have sought increase of the compensation.

3. Counsel for respondent No.3 has however, opposed the appeal by submitting that the appellants are not entitled to any enhancement as the claim petition was preferred by them under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act').
4.
I have heard counsel for the parties and considered their respective submissions.

5. The question that arises for consideration is as to whether the appellants are entitled to enhancement of compensation in an appeal challenging an award passed on a petition filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

In Deepal Girishbhai Soni and others Versus United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Baroda, (2004) 5 Supreme Court Cases 385 Supreme Court has held that an award passed under Section 163-A ibid is in full and final settlement of the claim and a claimant cannot be permitted to pursue two remedies simultaneously.

entities.text: Deepal Girishbhai Soni and others Versus United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Baroda, (2004) 5 Supreme Court Cases 385
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apex Court has clarified that the claimants can opt or elect to go either for proceeding under Section 163-A or under Section 166 of the Act but not under both the provisions.

It has been observed that Section 163-A lays down a comprehensive scheme for the purpose of grant of adequate 2 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:002639 compensation to a section of the victims, who would require the amount of compensation without fighting any protracted litigation.

Such an amount is final and cannot be permitted to the adjusted.
6.
In view of the settled legal position, there is no merit in appeal, which is dismissed with no order as to costs.
